title: Foods Rich in Vitamin K and Why You Need Them Daily
description: The clotting and bone vitamin. Understand the difference between K1 and K2 and where to find them.
content:
Vitamin K is often overlooked, but it is essential for survival. It comes in two main forms: K1 (Phylloquinone) from plants, which is critical for blood clotting, and K2 (Menaquinone) from animal/fermented foods, which directs calcium into bones and away from arteries. Deficiency in K1 leads to bruising; deficiency in K2 is linked to osteoporosis and heart disease. A balanced diet must include sources of both.

Key Takeaways

  • Leafy Greens (Kale, Spinach) are the kings of Vitamin K1.
  • Natto (fermented soy) is the highest known source of Vitamin K2.
  • Vitamin K is fat-soluble; eating greens without fat (dressing) means you absorb almost none of it.
  • Antibiotics can deplete Vitamin K stores by killing the gut bacteria that produce small amounts of it.

Why It Matters

If you take Calcium and Vitamin D for your bones but skip Vitamin K2, you might be doing more harm than good. K2 acts as the traffic cop, ensuring that calcium lands in your skeleton, not your heart valves. It is a crucial piece of the longevity puzzle.

The Green Giants (K1)

Kale, Collard Greens, and Spinach are packed with K1. One cup of cooked kale provides over 1000% of your daily value. However, since it is fat-soluble, you must sauté these greens in oil or eat them with avocado to actually absorb the vitamin.

The Fermented Superfood (K2)

Natto is a Japanese breakfast dish of fermented soybeans. It has a strong smell but is the most potent source of K2 (MK-7) on earth. If you can't stomach it, Hard Cheeses (like Gouda/Brie) and Egg Yolks contain smaller, but useful amounts.

The Liver Connection

Beef Liver and Goose Liver are rich in K2 (MK-4). This form is rapidly absorbed and used by tissues. For those on a carnivore or paleo diet, organ meats are the primary source of this critical nutrient.

Workflow

  1. Oil Your Salad: Never eat a dry salad. A vinaigrette with olive oil increases Vitamin K absorption from the lettuce by up to 300%.
  2. Eat the Yolk: Egg whites have no Vitamin K. The yolk has K2. Eat the whole egg to support bone and heart health.
  3. Consider a Supplement: If you don't eat natto or organ meats, a K2 supplement (MK-7) is often recommended, especially if you also take Vitamin D.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does cooking destroy Vitamin K?

No, it is very heat stable. Cooking spinach actually concentrates the nutrient because the leaves shrink, allowing you to eat more.

I'm on blood thinners, can I eat salad?

Consult your doctor. Warfarin works by blocking Vitamin K. Sudden changes in green intake can interfere with the drug. Consistency is key.
